misconceptions: TypeScript types are checked at runtime
interface and type are completely interchangeable
any and unknown are the same thing

templates.question: What is the difference between an interface and a type alias in TypeScript, and when would you use each?
keyPoints: Both describe object shapes and are mostly interchangeable for objects
An interface can be extended with extends and merged by declaring it again (declaration merging), for example to augment library types
A type alias can name unions, intersections, tuples, primitives and mapped or conditional types
A common convention: interfaces for object contracts, type aliases for unions and compositions
Both exist only at compile time

templates.question: What is the difference between any, unknown and never?
keyPoints: any switches off type checking for the value: anything can be assigned to it and anything done with it
unknown accepts any value but must be narrowed before it is used, which makes it the safe type for untrusted input
never has no values: a function that always throws, or a branch that cannot happen
Assigning to never in the default branch of a switch makes the compiler report union members that are not handled

templates.question: What are union and intersection types? What can you do with a value of type A | B without narrowing it?
keyPoints: A union A | B is a value of one of the types
Without narrowing, only the members common to every type of the union can be used
An intersection A & B has the members of both types
Intersecting incompatible types, such as string & number, gives never
A discriminated union uses a shared literal property to tell its members apart

templates.question: A function expects a UserId, but the code passes an OrderId and the compiler accepts it, which causes a bug. Both are type aliases of string. Why, and how can the types prevent it?
keyPoints: TypeScript is structurally typed: types with the same structure are compatible
A type alias does not create a new type, so both are plain string
A branded type such as string & { readonly __brand: 'UserId' } makes them incompatible
Values of a branded type are created by a validating constructor function

misconceptions: A type assertion with as checks the value at runtime
The compiler verifies that a user-defined type guard is correct

templates.question: What is type narrowing in TypeScript? Which constructs narrow a union type?
keyPoints: The compiler refines the type of a value inside a branch, based on control flow
typeof narrows primitives (typeof null is 'object'), instanceof narrows classes, in narrows by property
Equality and truthiness checks narrow, and so do checks of a discriminant property
Assignments narrow too, and the narrowing can be lost inside callbacks

templates.question: Model the state of a data request that can be idle, loading, successful with data, or failed with an error, so that invalid combinations cannot be represented.
keyPoints: A discriminated union with a literal status property, one member per state
Data exists only on the success member and the error only on the error member
Switching on status narrows each case
An exhaustive check with never catches states that are not handled
This prevents impossible states that separate isLoading, data and error fields allow

templates.question: How do user-defined type guards (value is T) work, and what is their risk?
keyPoints: A function that returns a type predicate value is T narrows the argument in the branch where it returned true
The compiler trusts the predicate and does not check the function's implementation
A wrong check gives a wrong type and errors at runtime
Assertion functions (asserts value is T) narrow by throwing
For external data a schema validator (such as zod) that derives the type is safer

templates.question: Code does const user = (await res.json()) as User and later crashes with "cannot read properties of undefined", although it type-checks. Why, and how do you handle API responses safely?
keyPoints: res.json() returns an untyped value, and as only asserts the type to the compiler
Nothing checks the data at runtime, so a different shape passes unnoticed
Treat the body as unknown and validate it at the boundary with a schema (zod, valibot)
Check res.ok and handle error responses before parsing the body
Handle optional fields explicitly

misconceptions: Generic type parameters exist at runtime
Every function with a parameter should be generic
Explicit type arguments are always needed

templates.question: What are generics in TypeScript, and why are they better than any for a reusable function?
keyPoints: Type parameters let a function or type work with many types while keeping the relation between input and output types
With any the result type is lost and mistakes are not caught
The type argument is usually inferred from the arguments at the call site
Example: function first<T>(items: T[]): T | undefined
Constraints restrict what the type parameter may be

templates.question: How do generic constraints with extends and keyof work? Write the signature of a getProperty(obj, key) function that returns the property's exact type.
keyPoints: T extends X restricts T to types assignable to X, so X's members can be used
keyof T is the union of T's property names
function getProperty<T, K extends keyof T>(obj: T, key: K): T[K]
T[K] is an indexed access type: the type of that property
An invalid key is a compile-time error

templates.question: Write the props type of a reusable Select component that works with any type of option and passes the selected option to onChange with its type.
keyPoints: A generic props type, for example SelectProps<T> with options: T[], value: T | null and onChange: (value: T) => void
Functions to get a label and a key from an option, since T is unknown to the component
A generic component function, function Select<T>(props: SelectProps<T>)
T is inferred from the options at the call site, so callers need no casts

templates.question: A generic function's result is inferred as string, or unknown[], where you expected specific literal types. What influences generic inference, and how can you guide it?
keyPoints: Type arguments are inferred from the arguments; with nothing to infer from, T falls back to its constraint or unknown
Literal values widen to their base type unless the context keeps them
as const, or a const type parameter (TypeScript 5), keeps literal types
Explicit type arguments or better constraints guide the inference

misconceptions: Partial makes nested properties optional too
Readonly makes an object immutable at runtime
Omit checks that the keys it removes exist

templates.question: How would you use Partial, Pick, Omit and Record to derive the types of an update request, a summary view and a lookup table from a User type?
keyPoints: Partial<User> makes every property optional, shallowly: an update payload
Pick<User, 'id' | 'name'> keeps chosen properties: a summary view
Omit<User, 'password'> removes properties; its keys are not checked against User
Record<UserId, User> maps keys to values: a lookup table
Derived types stay in sync when User changes

templates.question: How are mapped types built? Write a type that makes every property of T nullable.
keyPoints: A mapped type iterates over keys: { [K in keyof T]: ... }
type Nullable<T> = { [K in keyof T]: T[K] | null }
Modifiers add or remove readonly and ? (-readonly, -?)
Keys can be remapped with as
Partial, Readonly and Record are mapped types

templates.question: What are conditional types and infer? How would you extract the type a Promise resolves to?
keyPoints: T extends U ? X : Y picks a type depending on assignability
infer introduces a type variable inside the extends clause
type Unwrap<T> = T extends Promise<infer R> ? R : T; the built-in Awaited does this recursively
Conditional types distribute over unions when T is a naked type parameter
ReturnType and Parameters are built with infer

templates.question: You want type-safe event names such as 'user:created' and 'order:paid', each with its own payload, and a handler map that must have a handler for every event. How would you type it?
keyPoints: A map type from event name to payload type, for example EventPayloads = { 'user:created': User; 'order:paid': Payment }
Template literal types such as `${Entity}:${Action}` can build the names
A mapped type { [E in keyof EventPayloads]: (payload: EventPayloads[E]) => void } requires a handler for every event
emit<E extends keyof EventPayloads>(event: E, payload: EventPayloads[E]) ties each name to its payload

misconceptions: Code that compiles cannot have type errors at runtime
strict mode changes the emitted JavaScript
strict mode can be turned on later at no cost

templates.question: What does the strict flag in tsconfig turn on, and why does strictNullChecks matter so much?
keyPoints: strict enables a family of checks, among them strictNullChecks, noImplicitAny, strictFunctionTypes and strictPropertyInitialization
With strictNullChecks null and undefined are separate types that must be handled, which catches the most common runtime error
noImplicitAny reports parameters and values that would silently be any
These options change type checking only, not the emitted JavaScript

templates.question: How would you migrate a medium-sized JavaScript codebase to TypeScript without stopping feature work?
keyPoints: Migrate incrementally: allowJs, then convert files one by one
Start with looser compiler options and tighten them module by module up to strict
Type the boundaries first: API clients, shared utilities, data models
Use @types packages or declaration files for untyped libraries
Run the type check in CI so the migrated code stays checked

templates.question: What are .d.ts files, and when do you need to write one?
keyPoints: They describe the types of JavaScript code without implementation
Libraries ship them, or the community provides them as @types packages (DefinitelyTyped)
You write one for an untyped library or for globals
Module augmentation extends the types of an existing library
They are used only at compile time

templates.question: The editor shows no errors, but the CI build fails with "Cannot find module" for an import that uses a path alias such as @/components. What would you check?
keyPoints: paths in tsconfig only teach the type checker the alias
The bundler, the test runner or Node need the same alias in their own configuration (Vite resolve.alias, Jest moduleNameMapper)
CI may build with another tsconfig, such as tsconfig.build.json
A case-sensitive file system in CI exposes imports whose case differs from the file name
